questions.question: Use calculate_correlation in order to know What is the relationship between Age and Cholesterol for patients with and without heart disease?

answer.value: The correlation between Age and Cholesterol is weak for both heart disease groups, with Presence group showing correlation of 0.158 and Absence group showing correlation of 0.227. This suggests that cholesterol levels do not strongly correlate with age in either group. However, patients with heart disease presence tend to be older (mean age 56.6 vs 52.7) and have slightly higher cholesterol levels (mean 256.5 vs 244.2), indicating that while age and cholesterol are not strongly correlated individually, both factors may contribute to heart disease risk when considered together.

Weak correlation indicates cholesterol levels do not strongly depend on age
Patients with heart disease tend to be older and have higher cholesterol
